# A pure js: function folds to a literal at build time: node runs it once
# during the compile and the result is spliced in, so the shipped page carries
# the answer rather than the call that computes it.
[!node] skip
env SNGL_CONSTEVAL_CACHE=$WORK/evalcache

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

grep 'HELLO WORLD' out/index.html
! grep 'toUpperCase' out/index.html

# A value crosses as SNGL source, and SNGL has no exponent syntax — `1e30`
# lexes as a unit literal — so a number outside the range JS prints without an
# exponent has its point moved by hand on the way out. Both ends of that range
# are here: written the way String() writes them, neither would parse, and the
# build would fail rather than fold. What the page shows is the number
# formatted for display again, which is not what is being asserted.
grep '>1e\+30<' out/index.html
grep '>1e-07<' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"
import lib "js:./lib"

const greeting = lib.shout("hello world")
const big = lib.big()
const small = lib.small()

component main {
    text(value=greeting)
    text(value=string(big))
    text(value=string(small))
}
-- lib/index.ts --
/** @sngl-pure */
export function shout(s: string): string {
    return s.toUpperCase();
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export function big(): number {
    return 1e30;
}

/** @sngl-pure */
export function small(): number {
    return 1e-7;
}
